text:
Maya: Quick idea — add a 'preview rollout' mode for runtime config. It would let us route a sampled percentage of traffic to new values, collect eval telemetry, and show console diffs before we flip fully. Thoughts? :thinking:
Jason: love it. two questions: how do we surface quota/route impacts during preview? and what's the API shape for overrides?
Li: we should avoid actually changing routing decisions that affect SLAs during preview. maybe a shadow-eval that runs the decision logic but doesn't alter billing or routing, just logs counters.
Maya: yeah, shadow-eval + dry-run flag. console shows "expected vs observed" for chosen route/quota. preview still needs to simulate batching and cache hit differences for perf estimates.
Sam: UX: in console show a side-by-side diff and a small traffic toggle (0.1% / 1% / 5% / 25%) + an option for "telemetry gate" that prevents promotion if certain signals regress.
Jason: telemetry gate needs a concrete contract. I propose a small set of signals: latency p95, error-rate (5xx/timeout), model-quality regression (eval set score delta). Gate thresholds should be configurable per rollout.
Maya: agreed. also add a emergency cutoff: if quota consumption or cost per token goes > X% compared to baseline, auto-pause.
Li: API idea: POST /configs/:id/preview with body {"value":..., "sample_rate":0.01, "gate_rules": [ {"signal":"p95_ms","op":"<=","threshold":450}, {"signal":"eval_delta","op":"<=","threshold":-0.02} ] }
Sam: console should expose the gate_rules UI builder. Keep defaults sane so Product can use quick-preview with a single click.
Jason: question: are previewed requests actually routed to the new model variant? If so, that affects capacity planning. If not, it's purely simulated. We need both modes: "simulated" vs "live-candidate".
Maya: yes two modes. simulated = run the decision/path on a copy of request (no billing, no real routing). live-candidate = route a tiny fraction to the real variant (will consume capacity). Console warns and requires a higher privilege to enable live-candidate.
Li: we must propagate a header in live-candidate like X-Config-Preview: live so downstream can opt-in to special logging and not count towards some quotas (where supported).
OpsBot: deployment note: preview endpoints created in staging and prod must tag metrics as preview.{config_id}.{signal} and route metrics to a dedicated dry-run namespace.
Maya: small sample config snippet for reference:
```json
{
  "config_id": "route_policy_42",
  "value": {"route_by":"latency-aware","cohort":"variant-b"},
  "sample_rate": 0.01,
  "mode": "simulated",
  "gate_rules": [
    {"signal":"p95_ms","op":"<=","threshold":500},
    {"signal":"error_rate","op":"<=","threshold":0.005}
  ]
}
```
Jason: nice. Implementation notes: need a lightweight sidecar to evaluate the config in prod path without blocking request path. OR evaluate asynchronously using an event-capture pipeline. Prefer non-blocking to keep latency SLOs.
Li: we can use existing tracing hooks to fork a copy of request to preview worker. That worker calls the same routing code but returns no routing action. We then emit metrics to the preview namespace.
Sam: metric UX: show rolling window and a delta vs baseline with an uncertainty band (because sample rates vary). Allow regression annotation and manual override to proceed.
Maya: rollout rollback: two auto-rollback triggers — gate thresholds and manual adoption rate stays < X after Y hours. Also allow immediate revert from console with one click.
Jason: edge-case: nested config overrides (per-customer). preview should support scope testing (e.g., only org=acme or user cohort). Add a field scope: {"org":"acme"}.
Li: security: only people with config:preview permission can create live-candidate previews. Log who started preview and link to audit logs.
OpsBot: note saved: #cfg-preview-proposal created, assigned to eng-platform/ops for spike.
Maya: OK I'll draft the API PR and mock console screens. I'll include default gate presets (safe/standard/aggressive). Thanks all. :thumbsup:
